The discipline of electrical engineering is the engineering science that moves electric charges in a controlled way in order to transmit energy and process information. A power plant, a motor, a wireless network and a processor all rest on the same process forces set charges in motion. Physics describes nature with measurable quantities and looks for the laws connecting them. The engineering sciences apply these laws, for example in components, circuits connections of components and power plants. All materials consist of atoms. An atom has a tiny nucleus of protons and neutrons , around which electrons move Fig. 1 abb 1 . Protons carry a positive charge, electrons a negative charge of exactly the same size, neutrons none. An atom contains as many protons as electrons; seen from outside, their charges cancel, and it is neutral . If it loses an electron, a positive charge is left over. An atom with a surplus charge is called an ion . Protons sit firmly in the nucleus and are 1836 times heavier than electrons, whereas outer electrons can be detached. That is why electrons are what moves in nearly all processes of electrical engineering. Diagram of an atom with three protons and three neutrons. Left, neutral three positive and three negative charges add up to zero. Right, one electron is missing the ion carries the charge . This stage settles the first question What is charge, how does a charged body come about, and what is conserved in the process? The idea. Frictional electricity, lightning as the discharge of separated charges through the air, and magnetism cannot be explained by mechanics. If a glass rod is rubbed with a silk cloth and a hard rubber rod with fur, the two rods attract each other, while two hard rubber rods repel Fig. 3 abb 3 . Rubbing creates nothing new; electrons change bodies. Different materials bind their outer electrons with different strength. At the points of contact, electrons pass to the material that binds them more strongly, and rubbing creates many such points. A body with an electron deficit is positively charged, one with an electron excess negatively. Top rubbing separates charge. Electrons pass from the glass to the silk and from the fur to the rubber. Bottom oppositely charged rods attract, like charged rods repel. A body with protons and electrons carries the charge The elementary charge is the smallest charge occurring freely. An electron carries , a proton . In a closed system, the sum of all charges stays constant conservation of charge . ⁠ How to read it Charge occurs only in multiples of ; one coulomb is elementary charges. Rubbed rods carry around 10 nC. Validity These steps are noticeable only for individual particles; even 1 nC is six billion electrons. In circuits, charge is therefore treated as a continuous quantity. Two bodies together carry . If an electron passes from 1 to 2, decreases by one and increases by one; the bracket stays the same. The charges “generated” by rubbing always add up to zero. The names are older than the electron. In 1733 DuFay distinguished vitreous and resinous electricity; around 1750 Franklin called one positive and the other negative. The Greek word for amber, elektron , gave the field its name. Conductors and insulators. In a conductor such as metal, at least one electron per atom can wander through the entire body. In an insulator such as glass or rubber, the electrons stay with their atoms. That is why charge on an insulator stays where it was produced, whereas on metal it spreads immediately. Coulomb's law gives the force but does not say how it gets across empty space. The concept of the field answers this and separates cause from effect. The idea. Instead of “B pulls A across 3 cm”, the process is split in two. First charge B changes the space around it; it produces a field. Second charge A feels the field at its own location and experiences a force there. Why charges produce fields cannot be traced back to anything simpler; it is a fundamental law. But the picture solves three problems. Cause and effect are separated The field depends only on the charges producing it and holds for any charge brought into it. Many charges become manageable Their fields are added once, and after that you calculate with one vector per location. The effect takes time If B is moved, the force on A changes only when the change in the field arrives there at the speed of light. Over 3 cm this takes 100 ps, from the Sun to the Earth 8.3 minutes. In the meantime, the change resides in the field, so the field is more than a computational aid. The Earth is surrounded by a gravitational field at every location, the force acts on every mass. The field is force per mass; the electric field is force per charge. The picture stops working in two places masses always attract, and a gravitational field cannot be shielded. If a small test charge is brought to a location and the force on it is measured, the electric field strength there is The direction of is the direction of the force on a positive test charge. What this is about Two metal plates with an insulator between them this component is called a capacitor . If you connect it to a battery, current flows in the leads even though the plates do not touch. The current grows weaker and stops by itself. If you disconnect the battery, the voltage remains, and the component can drive current on its own. The question of this chapter is How can current flow into an insulator, why does it end by itself, and where is the energy afterward? Each plate is an electrode ; the insulator between them is called the dielectric . The quantity that characterizes the component is the capacitance it says how much charge sits on the plates per volt. The basic form is two flat plates, the parallel plate capacitor . In a pointer instrument, a rotatable coil of thin wire sits between the poles of a permanent magnet Fig. 1 abb 1 . When current flows, the magnetic field exerts a force on the moving electrons in the wire, and the coil turns against a spiral spring. The torque grows with the current, the counterforce of the spring with the angle. That is why the deflection is proportional to the current. A network with four terminals has three independent currents and three independent voltages. This stage shows which condition turns these into two currents and two voltages. The idea. The mesh rule likewise ties together the voltages between the terminals. Now if a two terminal element, say a source, is connected to terminals 1 and 1 , a further statement is added A two terminal element has only two connections. Every charge it gives off at one it takes back at the other. The current that enters the network at terminal 1 must return at terminal 1 . A two port is a conceptually closed unit, accessible only through its ports. Its properties are fixed by the relations between the port quantities, and these can be calculated or measured. Usually a source is connected to port 1, the input , and a load to port 2, the output . Energy then flows in the forward direction ; the opposite direction is called the reverse direction . The two port is a basic structure Controlled sources are two ports, transformers, amplifiers and transistors have three or four connections, large two ports can be built from elementary two ports , and two ports joined together form a two port again. In n doped silicon, electrons are free to move; in p doped silicon, holes are missing electrons that move like positive charges. At the boundary between the two regions, the pn junction , the space charge region forms a strip with almost no free carriers, in which fixed ions produce an electric field from the n region to the p region. This field acts as a barrier for the majority carriers of each side. Plus at the p region lowers it, and the diode conducts in the forward direction . Plus at the n region raises it, and the diode blocks. Diffusion is the motion of particles from a dense place to a sparse one; recombination is the encounter of an electron with a hole, in which both disappear as free carriers. What this is about An operational amplifier , op amp for short, is an integrated amplifier made of a few dozen transistors. It amplifies the voltage between its two inputs by a factor of about 100000. This factor is called the open loop gain . It varies by a factor of four from one specimen to the next and changes with temperature. Nevertheless, this component is used to build amplifiers that feel only 0.01 % of this variation, as well as summing amplifiers and integrators. The question is How does a huge, imprecise factor turn into a component whose behavior is determined by the resistors alone?
